papers.title: Preparation of powder from Ti-6Al-4V chips by self-propagating high-temperature synthesis hydrogenation and thermal dehydrogenation
papers.abstract: The paper proposes a novel method for processing Ti-6Al-4V titanium chips into fine powder using self-propagating high-temperature synthesis (SHS)-hydrogenation technology and subsequent thermal dehydrogenation. It was found that SHS-hydrogenation leads to the formation of single-phase titanium hydride with a cubic crystal lattice. Subsequent grinding of the brittle hydrogenated chips in a ball mill produced a powder with a particle size of 10–40 μm and an angular shape. Thermal dehydrogenation in vacuum resulted in a powder with equilibrium fine (α + β) structure (grain length 2–3 μm, thickness ≤1 μm) and residual hydrogen content of 0.015 wt.%. The effectiveness of the developed methodology is demonstrated by the ability to produce powders with minimal impurity content and a controlled microstructure, thus providing an effective solution to the problem of recycling titanium waste. The results of the work are of practical interest for additive manufacturing and powder metallurgy of titanium.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及Ti-6Al-4V粉末制备，但未提供任何力学或疲劳性能数据，与用户关注的力学与疲劳方向相关性较弱。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on powder production from Ti-6Al-4V chips via hydrogenation and dehydrogenation, with no mechanical or fatigue testing, thus falling outside the mechanical/fatigue characterization scope of Layer 1.

summary_zh.motivation: 提出利用SHS氢化技术将Ti-6Al-4V切屑转化为粉末的方法。
summary_zh.method: 通过SHS氢化、球磨粉碎和真空脱氢制备细粉。
summary_zh.result: 获得粒度为10–40微米、残余氢0.015 wt.%的粉末，具有细晶(α+β)组织。
summary_zh.validation: 通过微观结构和成分分析验证。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a method for recycling Ti-6Al-4V machining chips into fine powder suitable for additive manufacturing.
summary_en.method: Self-propagating high-temperature synthesis hydrogenation followed by ball milling and vacuum thermal dehydrogenation.
summary_en.result: Powder with particle size 10-40 μm and fine equiaxed α+β microstructure was obtained with residual hydrogen of 0.015 wt.%.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural and compositional characterization confirmed the process effectiveness.
